historical_notes.significance: Classic evidence for light-speed invariance, though its influence on Einstein is doubtful.

historical_notes.event: Unequal-arm interferometer showed round-trip light time independent of apparatus velocity as well as orientation.
historical_notes.significance: Complements Michelson-Morley; ancestor of modern cavity tests.

historical_notes.event: Doppler-shift measurements on fast ions revealed time dilation.
historical_notes.significance: First direct laboratory confirmation of time dilation.

historical_notes.event: Modern Kennedy-Thorndike-type test comparing a cavity-stabilized laser with a molecular reference (Phys. Rev. Lett. 88, 010401).
historical_notes.significance: Example of precision tests of light-speed independence from lab velocity.

historical_notes.event: Compared two Al+ optical clocks, one with a moving ion, detecting time dilation at speeds around 10 m/s (Science 329, 1630).
historical_notes.significance: Time dilation at everyday speeds with 1e-17 frequency precision.

historical_notes.event: Review of experimental tests of Lorentz invariance (Class. Quantum Grav. 30, 133001).
historical_notes.significance: Source for the statement that no significant violation has been found.

applications_and_observations.details: Round-trip light times along interferometer arms show no dependence on orientation (equal arms, 1887) or on apparatus velocity (unequal arms, 1932).

One laser locked to a molecular absorption line, another to a Fabry-Perot cavity with frequency n c(v)/(2l); their beat frequency is monitored as Earth's orbital velocity changes, which would reveal any velocity dependence of c.
applications_and_observations.key_numbers: nu_cav = n c(v)/(2 l); Braxmaier et al. 2002

applications_and_observations.details: Doppler shifts of light from accelerated ions reveal time dilation; modern versions use heavy-ion storage rings and laser spectroscopy.

Two Al+ clocks, one with its ion driven to move by a static electric field; frequency comparison at the 1e-17 level agrees with time dilation. Own estimate: at v = 10 m/s the fractional shift v^2/2c^2 is about 6e-16, comfortably above that precision.
applications_and_observations.key_numbers: v about 10 m/s; precision 1e-17; expected shift about 5.6e-16 (own estimate)

applications_and_observations.details: Muons created by cosmic rays in the upper atmosphere reach the ground thanks to time dilation (or atmospheric contraction in the muon frame); accelerator muon beams test the same effect.
applications_and_observations.key_numbers: Rest lifetime 2.2 microseconds; naive range about 0.7 km

applications_and_observations.details: Own worked numbers for the exercise: gamma is about 10.0; mean range without dilation about 0.66 km, with dilation about 6.6 km, enough to reach the ground from typical production altitudes.
applications_and_observations.key_numbers: gamma(0.995) about 10.01; 657 m vs 6.57 km (own estimate)

applications_and_observations.topic: Speeds needed for sizable relativistic corrections (Exercise 1.4)
applications_and_observations.details: Own solution values: gamma - 1 = 0.01 needs beta about 0.14; 0.1 needs about 0.42; 1 needs about 0.87; 10 needs about 0.9959; 100 needs about 0.99995.
Own illustrative numbers for Example 1.6: with x* about 4.24 light years and v = 0.8c (gamma = 5/3), the Earth twin ages about 10.6 years and the traveller about 6.4 years.
A large body of experiments searching for violations of boost and rotation symmetry has found none of significance (review by Liberati, 2013).
Relied upon in particle accelerator design, astrophysics, telecommunications, space missions and condensed matter physics.

notation_and_conventions.convention: Squared interval ds^2 = -c^2dt^2 + dx^2 + dy^2 + dz^2 (-+++), the convention of most GR textbooks.
notation_and_conventions.notes: Opposite to the authors' own QFT book and particle physics generally (+---).

notation_and_conventions.convention: Spacelike Delta s^2 > 0, null Delta s^2 = 0, timelike Delta s^2 < 0.
notation_and_conventions.notes: Follows from the -+++ choice; reversed in +--- texts.

notation_and_conventions.convention: dx^2 means (dx)^2, brackets dropped for brevity.
ds^2 is often loosely called the interval, although strictly the interval is ds.
notation_and_conventions.notes: Squared form avoids square roots of negative numbers.

notation_and_conventions.convention: SI-style with c kept explicit throughout the chapter; time coordinates enter as ct.
notation_and_conventions.notes: No c = 1 units in this chapter.

notation_and_conventions.convention: Column vectors are written (x, ct) with the space component on top, and the primed frame S' moves at +v relative to S.
notation_and_conventions.notes: Many texts order (ct, x) with time as the 0th component; entries then appear permuted.

notation_and_conventions.convention: The boost is written with +sinh theta entries so that beta = -tanh theta.
notation_and_conventions.notes: Several margin notes (15, 18, 24) then carry an inconsistent minus sign in beta; only magnitudes matter there.

notation_and_conventions.convention: Delta denotes finite coordinate differences (valid in flat spacetime), d denotes infinitesimal ones.
tau is proper time; lambda = a tau + b is an affine parameter.
notation_and_conventions.notes: In eqn 1.18 alpha and beta label endpoint events, not the velocity ratio beta.

notation_and_conventions.convention: Primed coordinates belong to frame S'; in Example 1.7 a prime on y means d/dx.
notation_and_conventions.notes: Two uses of the prime in close succession.

notation_and_conventions.convention: In eqn 1.25 s denotes Euclidean path length, reusing the symbol of the spacetime interval.

margin_notes.summary: Epigraph from Oscar Wilde's The Picture of Dorian Gray mocking a slow death by common sense, setting the tone for dismantling intuitive beliefs.
Correcting for signal travel time to a space station would still, naively, let everyone agree two sandwich bites were simultaneous.
Timing a train trip from the station requires a signal of the departure time and a delay correction.
Measuring a moving train's length from the platform needs both ends located at one instant; harder in practice, fine in principle, and naively expected to agree with the onboard tape measure.
The mechanical-wave-in-ether assumption raised the difficulties; see Cheng for the history.
Reminder of the definition of an inertial frame: a frame with zero acceleration.

Defines an event as a single point of spacetime, an occurrence pinned to one location and one instant, illustrated with everyday and microscopic happenings such as a photon being emitted or a balloon popping.

Sign-convention warning: QFT (including the authors' own QFT book) uses c^2dt^2 - dx^2 - ...; this book follows most GR texts; compared to driving on the left in some countries and the right in others.
The proportionality ds^2 = a ds'^2 is justified by null intervals staying null in all frames.
Notation: a squared differential such as dx^2 stands for (dx)^2; the brackets are dropped because the expression recurs constantly.
Explains working with ds^2 instead of ds (no square roots of negative quantities) and that 'the interval' is commonly used loosely for the squared quantity.
The relative speed in the three-frame argument is the magnitude of the velocity difference, v12 = |v1 - v2| (a Galilean expression; see gaps).
Einstein's 1905 paper considered only flat spacetime.
Component form x' = gamma(x - vt), t' = gamma(t - vx/c^2) of the boost matrix.
Defines beta as v/c (the in-text note marker is missing from the text export but the note itself is present).
One-line proof that a simultaneity frame exists only for spacelike pairs (|beta| < 1).
Casualty notes on p.16: common-sense points 1 and 2 are abandoned once the extended present is established, and point 4 goes with Lorentz contraction (point 3 is dispatched on p.17).
The boost preserves the full four-dimensional squared interval; the example keeps only one spatial dimension for simplicity.
Time dilation obtained directly by boosting to the frame where the events share a location.
Cosmic-ray muons survive to the ground because of time dilation, or in their own frame because the atmosphere is Lorentz contracted.
Reassurance that the twin 'paradox' will turn out to involve no real contradiction.
Attached to the proper-time-along-a-path result: common-sense point 3 (universal durations) is now declared dead as well.
A clock may be a watch, a radioactive source, or the observer's own ageing.
The stationarity condition may give a minimum, a maximum, or (important in more dimensions) a saddle point.
The frame used in the maximal-time proof moves with velocity of magnitude x/t, giving gamma = [1 - (x/ct)^2]^(-1/2).
'Affine' derives from Latin affinis, meaning related or connected.
Michelson-Morley was known to Einstein but may not have shaped his thinking much; Cheng discusses his motivations.
Literature pointers: Braxmaier et al. 2002 (cavity test), Chou et al. 2010 (Al+ clocks), Liberati 2013 (Lorentz-invariance review).

difficulty.notes: Mathematics is limited to 2x2 matrices, hyperbolic identities, square roots and a standard calculus-of-variations derivation. The conceptual load is in abandoning simultaneity and reading spacetime diagrams, which the chapter handles briskly for a reader who has met special relativity before; a true first-timer would want more diagrams of tilted axes and more worked numbers. Several small printed slips (duplicated (dx)^2 in eqns 1.17-1.18, a sign in dF/dy', and inconsistent beta signs in margin notes) do not affect results but can confuse careful readers.

teaching_gems.gem: Present the Lorentz boost as a rotation with one sign flipped: same matrix template, cos/sin become cosh/sinh, cos^2+sin^2=1 becomes cosh^2-sinh^2=1.
teaching_gems.why_effective: Learners already trust rotations; the boost inherits meaning, and invariance of the interval becomes as natural as invariance of distance.
teaching_gems.app_idea: Linked rotation and boost panels sharing one angle slider, with a sign toggle that morphs circles into hyperbolae and perpendicular axes into scissoring axes.

teaching_gems.gem: Open with a numbered list of 'obvious' beliefs and strike each one off in a margin note at the moment the result that refutes it is derived.
teaching_gems.why_effective: Turns the chapter into a narrative with payoffs and gives the learner a checklist for what relativity changes.
teaching_gems.app_idea: Belief tracker sidebar: four cards that crack and flip to the replacing concept when the learner completes the relevant demo.

teaching_gems.gem: Redraw 'now' as the whole region outside the light cone (the 'extended present'), noting that the past and future are accessible but the present is not.
teaching_gems.why_effective: A memorable paradoxical slogan backed by a picture that directly replaces the naive Fig. 1.1.
teaching_gems.app_idea: Simultaneity-line sweeper where tilting lines of constant t' paint out the two spacelike wedges.

teaching_gems.gem: Solve the twin paradox entirely in the Earth frame, trusting invariance, and point out that the longer-looking path has less time because of the minus sign.
teaching_gems.why_effective: Avoids acceleration mysticism and frame-hopping; one clean calculation plus one visual paradox to remember.
teaching_gems.app_idea: Twin diagram where the learner stretches B's path; an on-page ruler shows Euclidean length growing while the proper-time clock shrinks.

teaching_gems.gem: Teach the calculus of variations on the Euclidean straight line, then apply the identical method to proper time and discover a maximum instead of a minimum.
teaching_gems.why_effective: Separates the method from the geometry and sets up geodesics as extremal proper-time paths.
teaching_gems.app_idea: Variational playground with Euclidean and Minkowski modes and a live I(epsilon) curve that flips from upward to downward parabola.

teaching_gems.gem: Define rulers and clocks operationally: a ruler gives length only with simultaneous end readings, a clock records proper time along its own world line.
teaching_gems.why_effective: Makes contraction and dilation consequences of measurement protocols rather than mysterious material effects.
teaching_gems.app_idea: Measurement lab: learner chooses when to mark each end of a moving rod and which clock to read; results are reported with the frame and simultaneity choices made explicit.

teaching_gems.gem: Tell the muon story twice: dilated lifetime in the ground frame, contracted atmosphere in the muon frame.
teaching_gems.why_effective: Shows two frames give different stories but agree on the invariant outcome, a key habit for GR.
teaching_gems.app_idea: Split-screen muon descent in ground and muon frames with a shared survival counter.

teaching_gems.gem: Measure the interval to a distant event with a single clock and a reflected light pulse: Delta s^2 = c^2 tau1 tau2 (Exercise 1.3).
teaching_gems.why_effective: Grounds the interval in something an observer can actually do without coordinates, previewing observer-based measurement in GR.
teaching_gems.app_idea: Radar-ranging widget: drag the distant event and see the emission and reception times and their product match the computed interval.

gaps_and_pitfalls.issue: Printed eqns 1.17 and 1.18 write (dx)^2 twice in the first line where (dz)^2 is intended.
gaps_and_pitfalls.impact_on_learner: Careful readers may think z drops out or doubt their own derivation.
gaps_and_pitfalls.suggestion: Use the corrected form with dx^2 + dy^2 + dz^2 in all app content.

gaps_and_pitfalls.issue: In the continuation of Example 1.7 the derivative of sqrt(1 + y'^2) with respect to y' is printed with a minus sign.
gaps_and_pitfalls.impact_on_learner: Harmless for the straight-line conclusion but undermines trust in the calculation.
gaps_and_pitfalls.suggestion: Show dF/dy' = y'/sqrt(1+y'^2) and note the result only needs it to be constant.

gaps_and_pitfalls.issue: Margin notes 15, 18 and 24 give beta (or the boost velocity) with a sign opposite to what eqn 1.13 as written requires.
gaps_and_pitfalls.impact_on_learner: Learners checking signs get contradictory frames; the underlying |beta| conditions are correct.
gaps_and_pitfalls.suggestion: State the conditions as magnitudes or re-derive with a consistent convention (beta = c Delta t/Delta x for simultaneity, beta = Delta x/(c Delta t) for co-location).

gaps_and_pitfalls.issue: The chapter says the straight timelike path 'maximizes the interval', but with the -+++ convention Delta s^2 is negative and is actually minimized; what is maximized is proper time (|Delta s|).
gaps_and_pitfalls.impact_on_learner: Sign confusion when geodesics are later written as extremizing an action with a particular sign.
gaps_and_pitfalls.suggestion: Always phrase the result as maximal proper time and write tau explicitly.

gaps_and_pitfalls.issue: Example 1.2's proportionality ds^2 = a(v) ds'^2 is justified only by null-to-null mapping, and the three-frame argument uses the Galilean relative-speed formula.
gaps_and_pitfalls.impact_on_learner: A mathematically minded reader may find the proof unconvincing; proportionality needs the forms to be quadratic and related by a linear map.
gaps_and_pitfalls.suggestion: Present it as a plausibility argument, or add the step that two quadratic forms sharing the same null cone are proportional, and note any correct relative-speed law still depends on the angle.

gaps_and_pitfalls.issue: Common-sense point 3 includes the claim that clock rates do not depend on altitude, yet the chapter declares point 3 dead after special-relativistic time dilation, which says nothing about height.
gaps_and_pitfalls.impact_on_learner: Learners may think SR explains gravitational time dilation.
gaps_and_pitfalls.suggestion: Flag explicitly that altitude dependence is a gravitational effect covered in GA ch6 §6.5 and measured by clock experiments.

gaps_and_pitfalls.issue: No diagram shows tilted primed axes, lines of simultaneity or the jump in the travelling twin's simultaneity at turnaround.
gaps_and_pitfalls.impact_on_learner: Relativity of simultaneity and the twin asymmetry remain algebraic; novices cannot see why each twin's reciprocal time dilation is consistent.
gaps_and_pitfalls.suggestion: Add interactive Minkowski diagrams with boosted axes and the turnaround simultaneity jump.

gaps_and_pitfalls.issue: The hyperbolic-angle derivation chooses +sinh entries, forcing beta = -tanh theta.
gaps_and_pitfalls.impact_on_learner: Negative angles for positive velocities add friction and conflict with most references, which use rapidity phi with beta = tanh phi.
gaps_and_pitfalls.suggestion: Introduce rapidity with beta = tanh phi and matrix entries -sinh phi; mention that rapidities add under collinear boosts.

gaps_and_pitfalls.issue: Relativistic velocity addition is never derived, even though the opening laser-chasing puzzle is about adding speeds.
gaps_and_pitfalls.impact_on_learner: The motivating puzzle is left unresolved quantitatively.
gaps_and_pitfalls.suggestion: Resolve it with rapidity addition: tanh(phi1 + phi2) gives (u + v)/(1 + uv/c^2), and show c combined with any speed is still c.

gaps_and_pitfalls.issue: Section 1.5 names experiments without the formulas linking measurements to effects (e.g. the Ives-Stillwell second-order Doppler shift or expected clock frequency shift).
gaps_and_pitfalls.impact_on_learner: Readers cannot judge the size of the effects being tested.
gaps_and_pitfalls.suggestion: Add order-of-magnitude estimates such as v^2/2c^2 for the Al+ clock test.

gaps_and_pitfalls.issue: Affine parameters are introduced for proper time only, without mentioning null world lines where proper time vanishes.
gaps_and_pitfalls.impact_on_learner: Learners may later wonder how light rays are parametrized.
gaps_and_pitfalls.suggestion: Foreshadow that for photons an affine parameter replaces tau (GA ch8 §8.4).

tutor_notes: Open by asking: 'If you and a friend on the other side of the planet clap at the same moment, would an astronaut flying past agree?' Let the learner commit before introducing relativity of simultaneity.
Ask the learner to list what they believe about time and length before starting; revisit the list after each demo, mirroring the book's four common-sense points.

Order: light postulate and laser-chasing puzzle -> Euclidean rotation invariance -> light sphere and ds^2 -> invariance of ds^2 -> light cone and interval classes -> boost as hyperbolic rotation -> simultaneity/extended present -> contraction -> proper time/dilation -> twin paradox -> variational maximal proper time -> affine parameter -> experiments.
Keep a sign-convention checkpoint: with -+++ spacelike is positive and timelike negative. Ask the learner to classify three events numerically before moving on.
Check understanding of length contraction by asking why a platform observer must mark both ends of the train at the same time, and whose 'same time' is meant.

When teaching time dilation, have the learner explain in their own words why 'moving clocks run slow' does not mean the clock malfunctions, and why the effect is reciprocal between two inertial observers.

For the twin paradox, first let the learner argue the symmetric case, then ask what an accelerometer on each ship reads; then compute both proper times in the Earth frame with concrete numbers (e.g. 0.8c to Proxima: 10.6 vs 6.4 years).
Common learner question: 'Isn't the longer path on the diagram longer in time?' Answer by writing d tau^2 = dt^2 - dx^2/c^2 and showing each spatial step subtracts.

Common learner question: 'Doesn't acceleration cause the ageing?' Emphasize that the difference grows with cruise duration at fixed brief accelerations; acceleration only marks which world line is not straight.
Flag explicitly that clock rates depending on altitude is true but gravitational (GA ch6), so the learner does not attribute it to special relativity.
Before the Euler-Lagrange derivation, confirm comfort with integration by parts; if weak, go straight to the intuitive 'wiggle the path and watch tau drop' demo and return to the derivation later.
Use the muon both ways (dilation in ground frame, contraction in muon frame) as a check: ask the learner to compute the atmosphere thickness seen by the muon for gamma = 10.
Warn about printed slips if the learner is reading along: duplicated (dx)^2 in eqns 1.17-1.18, the sign of dF/dy' on p.19, and beta sign flips in margin notes 15, 18, 24.
For advanced learners, extend with rapidity addition to resolve the laser-chasing puzzle and with the radar-ranging result Delta s^2 = c^2 tau1 tau2 as an operational definition of the interval.
